describes: The deontic plane's nD system: the axes a deontic statement occupies when it is carried as coordinates (operator, Hohfeld incident, bearer, action, counterparty, condition, exception, exception_status, negated), with the form-slot binding rules for a deontic claim. Published as data for any nD store (the versum reads it through the loomground.planes entry point); version equals the language version. Closed vocabularies equal vocabulary/operators.json and vocabulary/incidents.json (held equal by the test suite). Round 4: the plane's 5D binding (deontic.plane.binding()) is {} — operators are ought; the 5D describes what is; a norm's content enters 5D through the factual plane. Round 5: the `action` axis (value_type concept_reference) is not a 5D channel and carries no dimension itself — it is a reference (item_id / concept reference) to the action-type entry the consumer creates from the claim's `spans.content` (the literal span of the regulated action/state in the sentence, published by deontic.plane.claim_for); the norm links to that entry by a structural 'embeds' link, never by asserting the action into the norm's own coordinates. Negation is recorded once, on the norm: the `negated` axis is the sole authority for a not/never clause over the operator's proposition (e.g. F is O(not-a), never carried as text inside `action`); an action-type entry the consumer creates from `spans.content` records the same polarity, consistently with the norm's `negated` value, never a conflicting one. Round 5 defect (a), generalised: a negation adverb after a modal ("not", "never", "at no time"), with or without interposed commas or an interposed phrase (e.g. "shall never, under any circumstances,"), lowers the modal to F (prohibition), with the negation adverb and any interposed phrase consumed by the matched cue so neither reaches `action` nor is duplicated onto `negated` — the same convention "must not"/"shall not" already carry. This plane is registered as an nD system on the versum index (the `loomground.planes` entry point, id `deontic`); its operators (O/P/F) carry no 5D dimension — a norm's content is the action-type entry a consumer creates from `spans.content`, linked to the norm by a structural `embeds` link, and the deontic `action` coordinate (`concept_reference`) merely references it.
